title: Ada and the Confession
premise: When archivist Sebastian Sandoval receives a confession letter postmarked the day after the cathedral's beloved canon's funeral—admitting to a death thirty years ago that was ruled an accident—they realize the crypt's locked door hides more than relics. As Sebastian traces the letter through the town's oldest families, they uncover that the canon spent his final decade quietly protecting the person who wrote it, and that Sebastian's own late mother was tangled in the original night. The confession turns out to have two authors: one guilty, one shielding. In the end, Sebastian must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the found family the canon built around the cathedral—choosing, finally, to belong to the town rather than merely catalog it.
about_author: Hazel Galloway is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent six years cataloging a cathedral's archives before turning to fiction. She writes quiet mysteries about small towns, old paper, and the people history forgets to file.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Ten years of filing the cathedral's records, invisible and content. The canon's funeral fills the nave; Sebastian watches from the choir loft, the one place they belong. Emotional beat: grief disguised as routine, and the first crack of loneliness in a life built on order.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A confession letter arrives, dated the day after the funeral, confessing to the 1995 death of a young organist, ruled accidental. The handwriting is achingly familiar. Emotional beat: dread blooming in the safety of the archive; the locked crypt door suddenly feels like a question.

chapters.title: The Canon's Second Drawer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Searching the canon's office, Sebastian finds a hidden key and a decade of letters to someone signed only 'W.' The canon knew. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with tenderness—the mentor who kept them safe was also keeping something.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Okafor, the canon's goddaughter and the town's funeral florist, arranges the memorial flowers and notices Sebastian watching her too closely. She lies smoothly about her whereabouts in 1995. Emotional beat: the reader's first unreliable narrator—grief weaponized into composure.

chapters.title: The Organ Loft, 1995
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Digging into the old accident file, Sebastian learns the organist, Tomas Reyes, fell from the loft the night before his wedding. Every alibi in the file is signed by the same five families. Emotional beat: the past as a locked room with too many keys.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Vestry
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The five founding families host the memorial dinner; Sebastian attends as the canon's archivist and is, for once, included. Each family offers a polished version of 1995. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging—Sebastian wants to be one of them, which makes them dangerous to trust.

chapters.title: The Letter Wren Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren burns a letter from the canon in her sink, unfinished. Flashback: at seventeen, she saw something in the crypt the night Tomas died and told the canon, who swore her to silence 'for her own protection.' Emotional beat: the weight of a childhood secret grown into an adult cage.

chapters.title: Crypt Key, Crypt Door
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Using the canon's key, Sebastian opens the crypt for the first time and finds Tomas Reyes's wedding ring hidden in a reliquary—never buried with the body. Someone has been visiting. Emotional beat: awe tipping into violation; the dead have been waiting.

chapters.title: The Alibi That Doesn't Add
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian maps the five families' statements against the 1995 weather records and church schedule. One alibi is physically impossible: Marguerite Halloran's. But the canon's letters to 'W' intensify right after. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by the fear of what the canon was protecting.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Roses
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The matriarch of the Halloran family tends her roses and remembers the night she covered for her son Daniel—whose car was seen near the cathedral. She believes she protected a murderer. Emotional beat: a mother's love calcified into thirty years of complicity.

chapters.title: Daniel Comes Home
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Daniel Halloran returns for the estate reading, charming and evasive. He asks Sebastian, pointedly, what the canon 'left in the files.' Emotional beat: menace in a cardigan; the town's golden boy knows the archive is the crime scene.

chapters.title: What My Mother Filed Away
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In a box of the canon's papers, Sebastian finds their own mother's name—she was the cathedral secretary in 1995, and she typed the original accident report. She left town soon after. Emotional beat: the investigation turns inward; Sebastian realizes they were always part of this story.

chapters.title: Wren and the Wedding That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals to Sebastian (and the reader) that she was Tomas's fiancée's little sister, and that she saw Marguerite—not Daniel—climbing the loft stairs that night, carrying the missing ring box. Emotional beat: a witness finally speaking, thirty years too late and right on time.

chapters.title: The Confession Has Two Hands
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Forensic comparison shows the confession letter is written in two inks, two hands: the canon began it, someone else finished and mailed it. The postmark date means the second author wrote it after the canon died—deliberately, to be found. Emotional beat: the mystery inverts; the letter is a message, not a surrender.

chapters.title: Threats on Archive Paper
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Daniel offers Sebastian a generous 'consultancy' to inventory and seal the canon's papers. When they decline, the crypt is found disturbed and a page torn from the 1995 register. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; Sebastian stops being a bystander to their own life.

chapters.title: Marguerite Breaks
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Confronted by Sebastian with the ring and the impossible alibi, Marguerite confesses the cover-up but insists Daniel only argued with Tomas that night—she saw him alive afterward. Someone else was in the crypt. Emotional beat: relief and horror entwined; the truth is a corridor, not a door.

chapters.title: The Night, Reassembled
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian reconstructs the full night: Tomas discovered the Hallorans' ancestor's theft of church funds documented in the crypt, went to confront the family, and fell—pushed by someone no one suspected. The canon's letters to 'W' were never about Wren. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of every certainty.

chapters.title: W
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren realizes 'W' was the canon himself—Wilhelm, his hidden first name—and that his letters were confessions to his own silence. He saw the fall and said nothing for thirty years, protecting the town, until guilt made him write. Emotional beat: the mentor's fall from grace rendered as tragedy, not villainy.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The second handwriting belongs to the canon's housekeeper, Rosa, who found his unfinished confession, learned the whole truth from his notes—and mailed it after his death because he'd lost his nerve. She also saw who was in the crypt that night. Emotional beat: quiet courage; the invisible woman finishing the visible man's work.

chapters.title: Climax in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian lures the killer—Tomas's own fiancée, Elena, who pushed him when he called off the wedding after learning of her theft—by announcing a public reading of the confession in the crypt. Daniel, sent to steal the file, is caught instead; Elena comes for the letter and confesses in front of the assembled families. Emotional beat: the archive becomes a courtroom; Sebastian, finally visible, holds the room.

chapters.title: Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The canon's will leaves Sebastian the archivist post in perpetuity, the crypt keys, and one instruction: 'file the truth where the town can find it.' Sebastian chooses to open the full record publicly, accepting the town's anger and gratitude alike. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not property but responsibility; belonging chosen over invisibility.

chapters.title: Alphabetized, Annotated, Ours
chapters.summary: Wren and Sebastian's alternating POV. A year later: the crypt is a memorial to Tomas, Elena is sentenced, the Hallorans fund the restoration, and Wren and Sebastian—now partners in the archive—file the last letter under R for Reyes. Emotional beat: found family formalized in paper and stone; the story ends where archives end, with everything finally in its place.
